subject: art-design
title: Sketchbook Development: Foundations
welcome_lead: Treat your sketchbook as a journey, not a scrapbook.
meta_desc: GCSE sketchbook foundations: research pages, primary vs secondary, artist studies.
final_note: Examiners want to see thinking — your sketchbook is the proof.

concepts.def: Personal book recording the project process.
Page exploring artists, sources and ideas.
Photo or image from someone else.
Practical response to another artist's work.

walkthroughs.body_html: Begin with a title page, a clear brief and a mind map. Number every page. Reserve the first few pages for the theme, then plan a rough rhythm — research, observation, experimentation, development, final outcome — across the book.

Primary sources are your own photos, observational drawings and notes. Secondary sources are images you found elsewhere. Examiners weight primary sources higher because they show first-hand engagement.

An artist study is more than a printed image. Copy a section in their media, then write annotations explaining what you noticed and how it might feed your own work. Practical artist studies prove genuine research.
